title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Pighius defense; pious ear refuses sins entered Christ
pass_a_gloss: PLAC: Pighius's reading could not be defended more carefully than the learned man does here—he leaves no stone unmoved to wrest from the orthodox the argument they draw against Pelagius and Pighius from 'through one man sin entered into the world.' He labors in vain; truth cannot be stormed. Why demand that compound εἰσελθεῖν differ in sense not at all from simple ἐλθεῖν? Or who can bear hearing that our sins entered into Christ, or that through us sin entered into him? Does not a pious conscience flee such speech?
pass_b_english: PLAC. Pighius's exposition could not have been defended more carefully than it is by the learned man in this place: for he moves no stone that he may wrest from the orthodox the argument which they are accustomed to draw against Pelagius and Pighius from the Apostle's words, through one man sin entered into the world. But he labors in vain. Truth cannot be stormed. What is it, why the learned man demands to be granted to himself, that the compound eiselthein differs in signification not at all from the simple elthein? Or who will bear one saying that our sins entered into Christ, or that through us sin entered into Christ? Does not a pious conscience flee such a locution?
source_text: PLAC. Non potuit diligentius Pighii expositio defendi, quam sit a viro docto hoc quidem in loco: nullum enim lapidem non movet ut extorqueat e manibus orthodoxorum argumentum, quod soliti sunt adversus Pelagium & Pighium ex verbis Apostoli ducere, per unum hominem peccatum introiit in mundum. Sed frustra laborat. Expugnari veritas non potest. Quid est, quare sibi dari Vir doctus postulet, compositum εἰσελθεῖν, nihil significatione differre a simplici ἐλθεῖν? Aut quis ferat dicentem peccata nostra introiisse in Christum, aut per nos peccatum intrasse in Christum? Nonne talem locutionem pia refugit conscientia?

choices.choice: Cannot say sins entered Christ; compound ≠ simple come
